summary: Directly compare, describe, and order common objects using length, height, width, or weight; describe differences.
Classify and sort up to ten objects by an attribute; count objects in each category and order categories by count.
Ask and answer questions using gathered information, observations, and appropriate graphical displays for everyday problems.
Identify numerals 0–20 and represent sets with those numerals.
Compare two sets up to ten using greater than, less than, or the same as.
Create, extend, and describe repeating patterns of numbers or shapes.
Use different strategies to add and subtract within 20.
Add and subtract fluently within 10 using varied strategies.
Decide whether addition and subtraction equations are true or false using the equal sign.
Find the missing whole number in an addition or subtraction equation.
Create, describe, and extend growing and shrinking patterns with steps of 1, 2, 5, or 10.
Describe, compare, and sort two- and three-dimensional shapes by their attributes.
Identify at least one line of symmetry in everyday objects.
Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares and name the fractional parts.
Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes may have different shapes.
Determine whether a group of up to 20 objects has an odd or even count; express an even number as two equal addends.
Use addition to determine the total in rectangular arrays of up to five rows and columns; write an equal-addends equation.
Round numbers up to 1,000 to the nearest ten or hundred.
Represent single-digit multiplication and division facts and connect the two operations.
Use place-value reasoning to multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of ten from 10 to 90.
Solve practical multiplication and division problems within 100 with models and part-whole strategies.
Add and subtract multi-digit numbers using place value and operation strategies.
Model and solve multiplicative comparison problems.
Multiply up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers or two-digit by two-digit numbers.
Divide up to four-digit dividends by one-digit divisors, including quotient and remainder contexts.
Explain a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator.
Compare and order fractions with different numerators or denominators.
Model addition and subtraction of fractions with unlike denominators.
Model and solve multiplication of a fraction by a whole number.
Explain when multiplying by a fraction makes a product larger, smaller, or equal to the whole number.
Model unit-fraction division by whole numbers and whole-number division by unit fractions.
